chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Adolphus Allsbrook, the Golden Gloves bassist gambler, in Chicago
summary: Milt tells of meeting Allsbrook, who asked for lessons, brushed through Milt's book and later beat up muggers in an alley.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: The first time I saw Adolphus Allsbrook was in Chicago. He came to.... He was a Golden Glove fighter. He was boxing. And he was a converted gambler, just insane for gambling. And he won he Golden Glove contest out there, and

he brought his bass along with him -- he'd tuck his bass under his arm like it was a matchbox, he was so big. And I was playing with Erskine Tate at the Savoy Ballroom, and he came and stood and listened, and he stood right in front of the bandstand, looking up there at me all night, you know. And I look at this cat. So he said, "Man, you're wonderful," you know. I said, "Thank you." So he said, "I'd like to study with you." I said, "Well, if you want to come by my house... I'm living with my mother, and if you want to come by my house, it's cool," you know. So the next thing, he comes by my house and brings his bass, and I open my book to show him -- and he ran through that book like it was a no-sense(?) quote(?) (?) or something.

So I asked him out of my house. I told him that nobody comes in my house and insults me like that! He says, "No, you do some things I really like." I said, "Yeah? You do some things I really like, so let's study with each other."

And he went out that night gambling, and the guys in Chicago, they... He won some money, and he wanted to leave. And he had to come through one of the alleys, and the cats tried to waylay him in the alley, but they didn't know he was a Golden Glove boxer -- and he left about a half-a-dozen of them laying out there in that alley when he left. He was that kind of guy. And he went home, back to Minneapolis;

and the next time we saw him was in Minneapolis.
But Danny, what about that scene...? I know, like, Perry Bradford is from Atlanta, Georgia, and he was always talking about what was happening in Atlanta. Also, Eddie Heywood's father was from Atlanta, and they had some things going on down there in Atlanta...
